key_insight: The study provides the first direct experimental observation of Kelvin-wave turbulence along a single vortex filament, confirming a weak-turbulence cascade mediated by six-wave resonant interactions.
engineering_relevance: This gives fluid and turbulence researchers a controlled experimental basis for understanding energy transport along vortex cores, relevant to classical vortices and quantum-fluid models.
method: High-resolution spatiotemporal measurements of a single vortex filament
Resolved Kelvin-wave dynamics across a broad range of scales
Compared measured wave-amplitude spectra with weak-turbulence predictions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports spectra consistent with the predicted weak-turbulence cascade and identifies six-wave resonant interactions as the energy-transfer mechanism.
watch_item: The results come from a controlled single-vortex setup, so extending the conclusions to strongly forced or fully developed turbulent flows may require additional validation.
paper_title: Experimental evidence of Kelvin wave turbulence along a vortex core
